title: Hamlet and the Soliloquy
objective: After this level you can explain why the soliloquy lets an audience hear a character think, using Hamlet.
summary: Hamlet hides his thoughts from the court behind a show of madness. Only his soliloquies, speeches spoken alone on stage, let the audience hear what he really thinks and plans.

cards.headline: Hamlet hides what he thinks from everyone. Except you.
cards.body: Early in the play, Hamlet tells the court he has "that within which passeth show": an inner self no outward show can express. Then he starts acting mad on purpose. The people around him can't read his mind. The audience can, thanks to one old stage device.

cards.headline: A ghost, a murder, a mask
cards.body: In Hamlet, written about 1599 to 1601, the ghost of Hamlet's father says he was poisoned by his brother Claudius. Claudius has since married Hamlet's mother, Gertrude, and taken the crown. Hamlet's answer is to put "an antic disposition" on: a show of madness to deceive Claudius and the court. From here on, everyone on stage is watching a mask.

cards.headline: Thinking out loud
cards.body: A soliloquy is a speech in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud while alone on stage, or while the others keep silent. The word joins Latin solus, "alone", and loqui, "to speak". Don't confuse it with an aside: a brief remark the audience hears but the other characters supposedly don't. An aside is a quick glance at the audience; a soliloquy is a whole mind at work.

mascot.line: People mix these two up. Aside: a quick line the others don't hear. Soliloquy: alone on stage, thinking at length.

cards.headline: What only you hear
cards.body: Alone at the end of Act 2, Hamlet drops the mask. He fears the ghost may be the devil, so he plans a test: actors will stage a murder like his father's in front of Claudius. "The play's the thing / Wherein I'll catch the conscience of the King." In Act 3 comes "To be, or not to be", Shakespeare's most famous soliloquy, as Hamlet weighs whether it's nobler to suffer life's troubles or fight them. Claudius never hears a word. You hear all of it.
